title: Varicella (chickenpox): lesions in different stages
vignette: A previously healthy 27-year-old man comes to the clinic due to fever and rash. The patient is a missionary who recently emigrated from South Africa with his wife and 3 young children. Four days ago, he developed a high fever and malaise followed by the appearance of multiple discrete macules on his face, trunk, and extremities. The lesions are pruritic and evolved into vesicles then pustules. The patient has continued to develop new vesicles as other lesions crust over and heal. The remainder of the examination is unremarkable. This patient's symptoms are most likely due to an infection with which of the following pathogens?

clues.text: high fever and malaise followed by the appearance of multiple discrete macules
clues.note: A prodrome of fever/malaise before a rash is typical of a systemic viral exanthem such as varicella (chickenpox).

clues.text: lesions are pruritic and evolved into vesicles then pustules
clues.note: An intensely pruritic rash progressing macule -> vesicle -> pustule -> crust is characteristic of varicella.

clues.text: continued to develop new vesicles as other lesions crust over and heal
clues.note: Lesions in DIFFERENT stages simultaneously ('crops') is the classic hallmark of varicella - and distinguishes it from smallpox (all same stage).

whatMatters: Fever/malaise prodrome then a pruritic rash with lesions in DIFFERENT stages at once (macules, vesicles, pustules, crusts) = varicella (chickenpox), caused by VARICELLA-ZOSTER VIRUS. Answer E. The 'different stages/successive crops' feature is the key discriminator (smallpox lesions are all in the SAME stage).
strategy: Anchor on 'lesions in different stages/crops' = varicella. Reject smallpox/variola (synchronous, same-stage lesions; eradicated), coxsackievirus (hand-foot-mouth: oral ulcers + hand/foot rash), HSV (grouped painful vesicles in one stage), and HHV-6 (roseola: high fever THEN rose-colored macular rash in infants).

eliminations.label: Coxsackievirus - hand-foot-mouth disease
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: coxsackievirus causes hand-foot-mouth disease (oral ulcers + vesicular rash on hands/feet). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: it favors the hands/feet/mouth and is usually non-pruritic, not a diffuse cropping vesicular rash. ✅ Correct if: oral ulcers + hand/foot vesicles in a child.

eliminations.label: Herpes simplex virus - grouped vesicles, same stage
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: HSV causes localized grouped painful vesicles (or, if disseminated, in immunocompromised hosts). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: it is localized and its vesicles are in the SAME stage, not a diffuse rash in successive crops. ✅ Correct if: painful grouped perioral/genital vesicles.

eliminations.label: Human herpesvirus 6 - roseola (no vesicles)
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: HHV-6 causes roseola infantum (high fever, then a rose-colored MACULAR rash) in young children. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: roseola has no vesicles/pustules and occurs in infants, not this adult vesicular rash. ✅ Correct if: high fever then a maculopapular rash as fever breaks in a toddler.

eliminations.label: Parvovirus B19 - slapped cheek (your pick)
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: parvovirus B19 causes erythema infectiosum ('slapped-cheek' malar rash in kids; arthralgias in adults). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: it produces a lacy/macular erythema, NOT a vesicular cropping rash. ✅ Correct if: malar 'slapped cheek' rash or symmetric adult arthralgias/aplastic crisis.

eliminations.label: Variola (smallpox) - synchronous same-stage lesions
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: variola causes a vesiculopustular rash. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: smallpox lesions are all in the SAME stage of development (synchronous) and it has been eradicated; varicella lesions are in DIFFERENT stages. ✅ Correct if: a synchronous, centrifugal rash in an eradication/bioterror scenario.

reasoning: Fever/malaise prodrome then a pruritic rash progressing macule -> vesicle -> pustule -> crust
Key hallmark: lesions in DIFFERENT stages simultaneously (successive crops)
This is varicella (chickenpox), caused by varicella-zoster virus
mechanism: Primary varicella-zoster virus (VZV) infection causes chickenpox, a highly contagious illness spread by respiratory droplets/direct contact. After a 10-21 day incubation, a prodrome of fever and malaise precedes a pruritic rash that begins as macules and rapidly evolves to papules, vesicles ('dew drop on a rose petal'), and pustules that crust over. The pathognomonic feature is that new crops keep appearing, so lesions are present in DIFFERENT stages of development at the same time - this distinguishes varicella from smallpox (variola), whose lesions are all synchronous (same stage). After primary infection resolves, VZV becomes latent in the dorsal root/sensory ganglia and can reactivate as herpes zoster (shingles) in a dermatomal distribution. Management is supportive (antihistamines) with acyclovir for high-risk/complicated cases; a live attenuated vaccine prevents it. The distractors are other exanthems: coxsackievirus (hand-foot-mouth), HSV (grouped same-stage vesicles), HHV-6 (roseola), and parvovirus B19 (slapped-cheek/erythema infectiosum).

difficulty.label: 🧠 Knowledge
difficulty.text: First Aid Micro > VZV: chickenpox (prodrome + pruritic rash, lesions in different stages/crops), latency in dorsal root ganglia -> zoster; vaccine-preventable; contrast smallpox (synchronous).

difficulty.label: 📖 Comprehension
difficulty.text: 'New vesicles while others crust' = lesions in different stages = varicella (not smallpox).

difficulty.label: 🔤 Vocab
difficulty.text: Unsure on exanthem, macule/vesicle/pustule, successive crops, or synchronous vs asynchronous lesions? Tell me which.

difficulty.label: 🨤 Distractor
difficulty.text: Smallpox = same-stage (synchronous); coxsackievirus = hand-foot-mouth; HSV = grouped same-stage vesicles; HHV-6 = roseola; parvovirus = slapped cheek.

difficulty.label: 🗒️ Other
difficulty.text: Bank: varicella = lesions in DIFFERENT stages (crops); smallpox = SAME stage; VZV latency -> shingles.

memoryHook: Chickenpox is a rash caught mid-argument - macules, vesicles, and crusts all bickering at once (different stages); smallpox marches in lockstep (same stage).
